name: uiux
doc: The UI/UX concern as a self-contained BOTH-faces plugin — the exemplar third plugin. Its JUDGMENT face (`judgment_face`: corpora/domains) is the styling-engine-AGNOSTIC design-decision domains (color, motion, visual-hierarchy, surfaces-elevation, wizards-flows, forms-inputs, lists-selection, validation-feedback, design-method), extracted from corpora-core; on import they are staged THROUGH the registered engine's ratify gate (containers auto-adopted, principles proposed as candidates), never written live. Note: `css` is NOT here — CSS/Tailwind authoring is a styling-engine IMPLEMENTATION concern (subject: coding, gated on `styling` not `has-ui`), belonging with the coding/web-frontend stack, not the design concern; it stays in corpora-core pending a styling-stack plugin. Its PRAXIS face (`provides`) is the process of founding and syncing a project's design libraries: the library-init / library-sync phases and their deterministic backing library_state.py, extracted from corpora's praxis-plugin; on import they snapshot into the project's own praxis/phases and praxis/scripts slots. A project that has UI moves this whole concern in — praxis face → slots, judgment face → gate — and gets both the design domains a design unit-of-work composes and the library phases that bootstrap/maintain them. Cores stay minimal and generic; a concern is a plugin carrying both faces. It lives OUTSIDE praxis/ (like plugins/routing/) so praxis-core stays free of any engine reference.
